findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: There were packages of reduced oxygen packaged tilapia that were observed to be thawed without being removed from their packaging. CORRECTED- The PIC and another club member were educated on ROP fish needing to be removed from packaging immediately after being thawed or prior to thawing. The tilapia was removed from its packaging during the inspection. The ROP fish that is kept in its packaging while thawing leads to a risk for botulism. Ensure that members are educated on this practice.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 11/17/2019.

The facility has two small ice machines located along the east wall of the kitchen. Inspector observed that both ice machines were heavily soiled with black and red mold along the baffles and upper surface of the ice bins. Person-in-charge was shown the areas of concern and states that maintenance of the machines has fallen off lately. The facility previously took one of the two ice machines out of commission during the cold season to simplify cleaning and maintenance but this practice has ceased. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces, including those contacting ice/water, are cleaned and sanitized often enough to prevent mold accumulation. A follow-up is issued for 11/21/2023 to verify cleaning of the ice machines has been completed effectively. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces are soiled:
(a) drain/drain hoses junction for ice machines (mold), 
(b) bottom of Coca Cola cooler at bar (debris).
Club appears to maintain most surfaces very well, but the aforementioned surfaces should be cleaned.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Several very large pots are stored on the floor to the left of the oven (some inverted, some right-side-up).  Elevate these pots at least 6" off of floor in a way that protects the sanitized surfaces.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
(a)  There are boxes of single-service items stored on the floor of the kitchen pantry-closet (REPEAT).  Do not store single service items, food, or sanitized kitchen ware directly on floor.
(b)  During inspection, a sleeve of plastic cups was found directly under the plumbing for the bar hand sink.  CORRECTED - cups were moved.  Do not store single service items, or food, under plumbing.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
